^SAMPLE = GSM5861372
!Sample_title = Urine_Cystitis_5
!Sample_geo_accession = GSM5861372
!Sample_status = Public on Feb 05 2022
!Sample_submission_date = Feb 04 2022
!Sample_last_update_date = Feb 05 2022
!Sample_type = RNA
!Sample_channel_count = 1
!Sample_source_name_ch1 = Urine, Cystitis
!Sample_organism_ch1 = Homo sapiens
!Sample_taxid_ch1 = 9606
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = gender: Female
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = age: 63
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = symptom_score: 17
!Sample_characteristics_ch1 = problem_score: 16
!Sample_molecule_ch1 = total RNA
!Sample_extract_protocol_ch1 = We extracted microRNAs (miRNA) from 500 μL urine sample using a nanowire-microfluidic device (1) (2). We fabricated the nanowire device by assembling ZnO nanowire scaffolds, COP resin microfluidic substrate, COP resin substrate, two stainless steel holders, and PEEK tubes. After assembling the device, the inlet PEEK tube was connected to a syringe pump (KDS-200, KD Scientific Inc.) to introduce urine and lysis buffer. On the other hand, the outlet PEEK tube was put in an RNase-free microfuge tube (Eppendorf AG.) to collect the flow-through urine and miRNA-containing solution. The miRNA-containing solution extracted with lysis buffer was purified using Wako microRNA Extractor SP Kit (FUJIFILM Wako Chemical Corporation) according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
!Sample_label_ch1 = Cy5
!Sample_label_protocol_ch1 = Extracted RNA was labeled with Cy5 using the 3D-Gene miRNA labeling kit (Toray Industries, Inc., Tokyo, Japan) following the manufacture’s instruction.
!Sample_hyb_protocol = Hybridized for 16 h at 32.7 C with rotary shake (250 rpm). Hybridization buffer and washing protocol was in accordance with the manufacturer’s instruction (TORAY Industries, Inc., Tokyo, Japan).
!Sample_scan_protocol = 3D-Gene Scanner (Toray Industries Inc., Tokyo, Japan) was used for scanning. Images were quantified by the software Extraction (Toray Industries Inc., Tokyo, Japan).
!Sample_data_processing = Background (BG) signals were subtracted from the raw signals by statistically inferring the true signal based upon the assumption of normal distribution for the BG signal and exponential distribution for the true signal (Irizarry RA et al., 2003). miRNAs with (BG-subtracted signal) > 2^6 with at least 50% of the samples were selected, and the other miRNAs were removed from the down-stream analyses. Quantile normalization was applied after BG subtraction and low-expression miRNAs removal. Log2 transformation was applied after quantile normalization.
